Class ItemDisplay

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<ItemDisplay>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.ItemDisplay
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class ItemDisplay extends AbstractPanelElement<ItemDisplay>
An item icon rendered at a fixed position with optional count overlay and durability bar. No interaction. Distinct from a slot — ItemDisplay has no sync, no storage binding, no mutation; it only renders.

Works in all three rendering contexts. Render-only element.

Two forms for the item content:

  • Fixed stack — pass an ItemStack directly.
  • Supplier-driven stack — pass a Supplier<ItemStack> for stacks that change over time.

Items are always square. The size parameter is a single int; width equals height. Defaults to DEFAULT_SIZE (16 pixels), matching vanilla's native item render size.

Count and durability overlays default to visible, matching vanilla item rendering. Consumers wanting an icon-only display (no overlays) pass showCount=false, showDurability=false explicitly.

Rendering delegates to vanilla's GuiGraphicsExtractor.renderItem and renderItemDecorations — MenuKit ships no custom visual of its own for this element.

int sy = ctx.originY() + getChildY();

    • size

      public ItemDisplay size(int size)
      Fluent resize sugar — sets the item render size in pixels (items are always square, so this is a single dimension) and returns this display for chaining. Additive to the positional constructors.

      Single-arg by design. The canonical widget resize signature is .size(int width, int height) (Button/Toggle/Divider/etc.). ItemDisplay is one of the two sanctioned deviations (the other is Dropdown/DropdownMulti .triggerSize(...)): items render square, so a second dimension would be redundant. See the size-shape convention note on AbstractPanelElement.
